_comment: W&B display name / tags / notes per run id of runs.tsv, (re)applied after every sync pass by apply_labels.py (an upload of an offline fragment can reset the name to the Megatron job name). Owners: the run's agent.

ambitious_v2_main.name: ambitious_v2_16k_QB
ambitious_v2_main.notes: Ambitious v2 at 16k: quantile balancing (EMA 0.9) + global aux loss 1e-5. Replaced: cap 0.78 allocator thrash (32 s/step), then the long-context restart. Not a main run.

ambitious_v2_64k.name: ambitious_v2_64k_QB
ambitious_v2_64k.notes: Ambitious v2 at 64k (p132.0059): quantile balancing (EMA 0.9) + global aux loss 1e-5. Healthy to step ~340, but QB hid a strongly unbalanced raw router (max_vio 35, 1,811 near-dead slots, up to 616 ghost slots). Replaced by expert-bias balancing (v2b, then v2c).

ambitious_v2b_64k.name: ambitious_v2b_64k_bias_seqaux
ambitious_v2b_64k.notes: Ambitious v2b at 64k (p132.0071, commit ad149a00): expert bias (rate 1e-3) + aux_loss 1e-4. At mbs 1 x 65536 aux_loss balances each micro-batch = one sequence (load_balancing_loss == seq_load_balancing_loss), the per-sequence balancing ruled out for a batch-1 model. Cancelled at step ~77, replaced by v2c (global_aux_loss).

ambitious_v2c_64k.name: ambitious_v2c_64k_bias_globalaux
ambitious_v2c_64k.notes: Ambitious v2c at 64k (p132.0075, commit 809ce46b): expert bias (rate 1e-3) + global_aux_loss 1e-4 (token counts over TP x DP x CP and the step's micro-batches; not the per-sequence aux) -- after quantile balancing hid an unbalanced raw router. 360 experts + Engram 80B [2,3,4] + sign hash, LDM + pab, seq 65536 / mbs 1 / gbs 1024, cap 0.80, NCCL 8, ENGRAM_STEP_GROUP 1, new blend without openthoughts-3, rolling save every 100. 1k-step stability check (exit at 1000).
